notes.title: Whispers in the Moss Shortlisted as Best Retro RPG of 2024 by PPG!
notes.content:
I'm happy to share that Whispers in the Moss has been shortlisted as one of the Best Retro RPGs of 2024 by Press Play Gaming! This recognition is part of PPG's extensive Game of the Year 2024 coverage.

The nomination places Whispers in the Moss alongside incredible titles like Temple of Aeryn, Gnomes and Knights, and the winner, SKALD: Against the Black Priory.

You can check out the full coverage here: [url=https://www.pressplaygaming.net/articles/2024/12/04/ppg-game-of-the-year-2024-19-the-best-retro-rpgs]PPG Game of the Year 2024 - Best Retro RPGs[/url].

Thank you all for your support—it’s an honor to be recognized alongside such amazing games!

Best regards,
– Tapio

notes.title: Whispers in the Moss Rated 90/100 by Finland's Leading Gaming Magazine
notes.content:
[b]I'm excited to share that Whispers in the Moss has been awarded a great 90/100 rating by Finland's top gaming magazine, Pelit, in their October issue, along with the prestigious "Pelit Recommends" stamp![/b]

The thorough two-page review highlights the game as a classic RPG adventure crafted with care, skill, and attention to detail. Pelit praised the unique visual style and polished systems, adding that "the story is not that bad either." The game's soundtrack was highlighted as a particular "crown jewel". Overall, Whispers in the Moss is said to set a new bar in terms of ambition for games with this kind of retro aesthetic.

Additionally, the game was also featured in two other Finnish magazines, Pelaaja and Skrolli, in their September issues. Always a pleasure to witness some textmode art in a print magazine, so if you're in Finland, be sure to grab a copy of each!

Best regards,
– Tapio

notes.title: Big 1.2 Update Now Live!
notes.content:
Hello everybody! Whispers in the Moss has just received its biggest update yet. The 1.2 update provides some new oft-requested features as well as tons of smaller tweaks and fixes. The game's demo version has also been updated, and it's now running on the same 1.2 build.

[b]Some highlights of the 1.2 Update include:[/b]

[list]
[*]New 'Defend' battle skill added
[*]Hunt Locations are now available in the World Map
[*]New Items/Eqp tab in the menu allows you to see all your equipment-type items.
[*]Burgand Falls area was expanded
[*]A new fancy mini-game added to the Colosseum
[/list]

For full patch notes, check below.

Best regards,
– Tapio

[h2]Update Notes (Update 1.2, August 18, 2024)[/h2]

[b]BATTLE[/b]

New 'Defend' Mechanic: Added a 'Defend' skill with a new sound effect. Defending blocks 50% of physical damage until the character's next turn. A defending character gains Willpower and takes their next turn slightly faster.

Veda's New Ability: Replaced Veda's 'Channel' ability with the new 'Fortuna' skill. This slots-style mini-game grants the party random buffs based on luck.

Gaston’s AXIOM Skill: Adjusted Gaston's second-level Focus skill, ZEROE—and renamed it to AXIOM for distinction. Added new visuals and a third bullet effect for AXIOM-powered attacks.

Increased Gold Stealing: Increased the amount of gold that can be stolen from enemies, with an even larger increase for bosses.

Removed Post-Battle Retrieval: Winning a battle no longer retrieves items or gold stolen during the fight, making enemy Steal skills more impactful.

Skill Mechanic Adjustments: Made minor adjustments to various other battle skills.

Willpower Carryover: Remaining Willpower now carries over to the next battle but resets to zero when loading a save. Willpower is visible in the Status menu outside of battles.

GUNFIRE/GRENADE Fix: Fixed a bug with the GUNFIRE/GRENADE enemy skill that prevented it from dropping a player’s HP below 1.

Veda’s Attack Sound: Slightly improved the sound effect for Veda's physical attacks.

Minor Fixes: Various other small adjustments and fixes.

[b]MENUS[/b]

Hunt Quest Availability: Added a feature to the World Map that shows unstarted Hunt Quests when browsing map locations.

New ITEMS/Eqp tab: Added a new tab in the Menu displaying a simple list of all your equipment-type items, which was previously unavailable.

Status Menu Layout: Swapped the locations of Gold, Karma, and EXP Stack in the Status menu for a clearer view of Gold during NPC interactions.

Level Up Screen Improvements: Enhanced the Level Up screen to include descriptions of stats, aiding less experienced JRPG players.

EXP Countdown Update: Added a tick sound effect for the post-battle EXP countdown, with the counter now also accelerating exponentially to reach zero faster.

Shop Screen Adjustments: Made minor visual tweaks to the Shop screens for better clarity.

Objective Text Polishing: Refined the 'Objective' texts in the menu.

Ultimate Equipment Sound Effect: Added a special sound effect when equipping any ultimate gear.

Item De-Equip Bug Fix: Fixed a bug where de-equipping an item could cause the item count to exceed 99.

Minor Menu Fixes: Addressed other small menu functionality issues.

[b]MAPS AND SCRIPT[/b]

Burgand Falls Expansion: Expanded the Burgand Falls map and added a unique battle background image for this area.

Store Signposts: Added signposts to various stores and inns to make them stand out more from other buildings across the world.

Armand Outskirts Save Point: Added a missing save point to the Armand Outskirts, which was absent during the player's first visit.

Dialogue Additions: Added new dialogue, mainly to support the update's new features.

[b]OTHER[/b]

New Mini-Game: Introduced "The Crooked Fortuna" at Adira's Colosseum. This slot machine mini-game uses mechanics similar to Veda's 'Fortuna' battle skill and offers cash prizes, items, and EXP.

Item Updates: Updated some item definitions and names for better clarity.

Stacked EXP Bonuses: Added stacked EXP Bonuses for certain endgame side quests that previously lacked them.

Event Sound Effects: Added sound effects to certain events that were missing them.

Chest Counter Bug Fix: Resolved a chest counter bug in one of the endgame areas.

NewGame+ Skill Bug Fix: Fixed a bug in NewGame+ Mode where previously acquired skills could be lost during the playthrough.

notes.title: July Sale is Here + Update 1.1 Released!
notes.content:
[b]Dear community! Whispers in the Moss has entered a two-week July sales campaign. We've also released the 1.1 update, so what better time to pick up the game than now![/b]

The 1.1 update will provide many important tweaks to improve the game experience further. For a full update log, check below.

While the game has received excellent feedback, I've been diligently taking notes on all the criticism, suggestions, and ideas too. By far, the thing that has received the most mentions in this regard is the UI and especially the clunky saving. The update provides an important fix with a Quick Save feature, quickly available as you step on any Save Crystal.

Another wish I've heard from many players regards the bestiary, and how it should be accessible in-game too. This turned out very challenging to implement since I had coded the bestiary system in a way that was not compatible with this idea. It took me a pretty long time, but I'm happy to announce that I did manage to squeeze it in eventually. The bestiary is now available from the 'Hunts' menu by pressing ENTER.

I added a new way to navigate the menus, but only after the release did I realize that it's not compatible with Steam's own hotkeys. So, SHIFT+TAB will now allow you to browse backwards in the field and battle menus, but it also activates the Steam interface. :-D This will be changed to CTRL+TAB in the next update.

I wanted to add native gamepad support too, but it will have to wait because I wanted to get this update out quicker. Anyway, there is some good news for SteamDeck users, as according to several reviewers and test players, the game should be functional with the SteamDeck, although you'll have to adjust the controls manually. I haven't tested it myself, and the game is not verified, but feel free to give the demo or the full version a try. There are also several third-party apps that allow game controllers to emulate keyboard input, but I do realize it's a clunky extra step for the player. Hopefully one for the future.

The 1.1 update does not include new story content. As far as I'm aware, only a handful of players have finished Whispers in the Moss by now, and I'm not aware of anyone approaching a 100 % run either yet, so additional content didn't seem relevant yet. If you think you're having a strong run, I'd love to hear from you! Feel free to share a screenshot of your Hunts/Skills/Status tabs or your Bestiary-% and show them off to fellow players (and me!).

Anyway, I hope you enjoy the new features. Keep those suggestions coming!

Best regards,
– Tapio

[b]Whispers in the Moss, Update 1.1, Released July 3, 2024[/b]

[list]
[*]Quick Save: Added a 'Quick Save' feature when stepping on a Save Crystal. Will save on slot #1.
[*]Quit to Desktop: Added a 'Quit to Desktop' option in the game menu.
[*]Bestiary Access: You can now view the bestiary in-game by pressing ENTER when the 'Hunts' tab is open in the menu.
[*]Venom Balance: Made Rosemary items much cheaper to balance the venom status effect.
[*]Venom Bug Fix: Character's HP amount in the menu will now update as a character takes field venom damage (the bug prevented the menu from updating, and you couldn't see the damage taken).
[*]Item Shop: When browsing for items in an item shop, you can now see the equipped status of jewel-type items.
[*]Improved Interactions: Increased the interaction/activation area for various places and objects.
[*]Fishing Minigame: Some balance and bug fixes applied to the fishing minigame.
[*]Capture Skill: Adjusted the success rate for Veda's 'Capture' skill.
[*]Steal Skill: Adjusted the success rate for Orion's 'Steal' skill.
[*]Bug Fixes: Numerous other small bug fixes implemented.
[*]Dialogue Fixes: Numerous small dialogue adjustments made.
[*]Balance Tweaks: Numerous small balance adjustments made.
[/list]

notes.title: Two Weeks In: Celebrating the Positive Reception of Whispers in the Moss
notes.content:
[b]Whispers in the Moss has been out for two weeks, and I want to thank everyone for the warm reception the game has been getting. The reviews and coverage continue to be overwhelmingly positive, so the niche is definitely real—now I just need to locate all the lost sheep. Say "baa" if you're one of them![/b]

The Steam reviews currently boast an incredible 100% recommendation rate, which comes from 13 reviews, 8 of which are from customers.

The game has also been reviewed by 22 Steam curators, with 17 of them recommending the game. The 3 informational reviews are also very positive in tone.

Another metric that I'm very happy about is the "Units Returned" metric on Steam, which stands at just 1%.

In addition, Whispers in the Moss has been covered by many websites, media outlets, and blogs, plus a couple of YouTube/Twitch streamers. Practically all of the coverage has been positive. I've listed some links below, and there are additional reviews currently being worked on.

Meanwhile, I'm working on the 1.1 update. There will be lots of small fixes and some features requested by players. One larger feature I'm considering for this update is native controller support, potentially leading to SteamDeck compatibility.

Thank you again for all your support! Stay tuned for more updates and keep sharing your feedback.
–Tapio

notes.title: "This game is an absolute gem" – Thanks for the awesome reviews!
notes.content:
Now that Whispers in the Moss has been out for a few days, I want to take a moment to thank everyone for the fantastic reception!

Releasing a game with such eccentric aesthetics in 2024 was a bit of a gamble, but based on your reviews, I'm thrilled to see how warmly the style has been received. Your positive feedback on the gameplay is particularly gratifying, as it was a major focus during the latter stages of development.

I've compiled some of my favorite quotes from your reviews so far. We still need more reviews, so I hope everyone who picks up the game can take a moment to share their thoughts too.

[i]"My first thoughts immediately point to the Dwarf Fortress intro but as a full game. A huge point of the charm is exploring this text art world. ... An excellent accompanying soundtrack as well."[/i] (Steam Review / Healthycheekums)

[i]"This game is an absolute gem - the ANSI interface is well crafted and a real throwback to the good old days of the 1990's but at the same time the music, gameplay and pacing nail the mid 90's sprite JRPG feel."[/i] (Steam Review / Casey Jones)

[i]"First ANSI art JRPG I've seen, and quite possibly the first one, full stop. It's obviously a labor of love, and if you are or were ever into textmode games, you will get a kick out of this. Equal parts ZZT, Zelda, Questron, Final Fantasy IV and GORILLA.BAS."[/i] (Steam Review / 1 health)

[i]"I think this is the first game in a while to just hit it off so flawlessly on so many levels."[/i] (Steam Review / sniffing.CVM)

[i]"Uncultured Games have outdone themselves with new release Whispers in the Moss. The ANSI/ASCII + text UI style is reminiscent of generational games but absolutely impressive in its execution. The scope of the game is just as impressive."[/i] (Steam Review / CSH Picone)

[i]"An enchanting journey through ethereal landscapes, filled with challenging puzzles, strategic turn-based combat, and an original, captivating soundtrack."[/i] (Steam Curator Review / Danmaku Disciples)

[i]"This lil baby oscillates between pixel art masterpiece and a truly fun turn-based RPG. A real crunched out labor of love; so many detailed aspects, sweet dungeon-y jams...and a pretty weird world..!"[/i] (Steam Curator Review / ziggy_'s gaming garage)

[i]"Turn based retro JRPG with a very unique art! Very nostalgic, reminds me of games I used to play as a kid. I think the music is heavily inspired by games like Live a Live, KH and RH, really cool!"[/i] (Steam Curator Review / Visual Novel & JRPG's Solace)

All the best,
Tapio / Uncultured Games

notes.title: After 12 years of development, Whispers in the Moss is here!
notes.content:
[b]Note! If you picked up the game, then it would mean a lot to me if you could take a moment to [u]drop a review[/u] as well. The reviews are very important to the Steam algorithm.[/b]

**
After twelve long years, I have fulfilled a childhood dream and released my own JRPG. Twelve years is a long time to work on one project, way too long, and if I started today, I’d do many things differently. Still, I’ve given this game everything I’ve got. Even when I consider the things I could’ve done better, I’m extremely happy with the end result. Most of all, I’m proud of myself for completing something so herculean.

Now it’s time to sit back and be happy, perhaps take a sip of that dwarvenale, and look towards the moon. As for the rest of you, go play Whispers in the Moss, now! ːsteamthumbsupː

[i]– Tapio / Uncultured Games[/i]

PS. The game's soundtrack is coming to Steam soon, so stay tuned!

notes.title: Whispers in the Moss is released tomorrow! Check out the game's official manual!
notes.content:
Woo-hoo, less than a day until Whispers in the Moss hits Steam! The game has been getting very favorable reviews from Steam Curators, with about 10 curators recommending it already. Nice!

To help players learn the ropes, we have created a 25-page manual for the game. It includes useful sections like "Getting Started," "Terms Explained," and a basic "Main Quest Walkthrough." So, if you feel lost in the game, be sure to check it out. The manual is available on the store page—just click "View the manual."

All the best!
Tapio

notes.title: Whispers in the Moss demo released on Steam!
notes.content:
The demo version of the game is now available here on Steam too. Get your day flowing with some retro vibes, and download the demo now!

The demo version includes the game's first chapter. You'll be able to explore the early areas, get to know the beginnings of the story, and complete a bunch of side quests.

If you decide to get the full version, you can continue from where you left off. It requires some manual work, though, as you'll have to copy the save file ("0.sav" if you're using saving on slot #1) manually into the full game's FF/SAVES folder. If you want to transfer the global settings and the bestiary stats from the demo, you'll also need to copy the "settings.sav" file similarly into the full game's FF/SAVES folder.

Cheers!
- T / Uncultured Games

notes.title: Check out Rock Paper Shotgun's amazing review of the Whispers in the Moss demo
notes.content:
Hello everybody! I've been working hard to get all the store pages up and running, as the game's release is closing in. The demo version of Whispers in the Moss will hopefully hit Steam as soon as possible. The demo includes the beginning of the story and the first few areas and boss fights. You'll also be able to transfer the save file from the demo version into the full game by copying the file in the full game's directory.

The main news today is Rock Paper Shotgun's amazing review of the Whispers in the Moss demo. Nic Reuben at RPS gave the demo a try, and the review that came out of it is both hilarious and also very positive.

[i]"Throughout this, the runaway synth bass does a great job convincing me that, yes, I am truly burning a giant monkey to death. I’d like to play more! The lovely thing about this kind of homage to a bygone era is that Whispers In The Moss retains a tantalising sense of inscrutability. That’s despite it being, as I’ve said, pretty easy to wrap your head around. Still, even if there’s not more than meets the eye here, it’s still a very perky and worthwhile bit of JRPG."[/i]

You can find the full review at [url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/a-solo-dev-worked-12-years-on-this-retro-jrpg-and-its-out-next-month]Rock Paper Shotgun's website[/url]

As I've mentioned before, I don't have too much resources for marketing, so if you like what you're seeing, please spread the word about the game. Thank you! :-)

Best regards,
T / Uncultured Games

notes.title: Whispers in the Moss will be released in June!
notes.content:
Hello everybody! It's me, Tapio, the developer behind the textmode JRPG Whispers in the Moss. Here are a couple of short announcements as we get closer to the release of the game.

[list]
[*][b]WHISPERS IN THE MOSS will be released in JUNE 2024![/b] First and foremost and I'm happy to announce that the game is fully finished, and [b]it will be released in early June 2024[/b]. I will still take a moment to improve some aspects of the game and complete some things further down the to-do list. The game has been fully playable from start to finish for about six months already, but I've spent the last months polishing it, adding some new features and creating even more content for the game.
[*][b]A COUPLE OF NEW TRAILERS.[/b] The game's store page has two new trailers, a regular one and a more gameplay-focused one, showing some of the early parts of the game. Go check them out!
[*][b]HOW LONG IS THE GAME?[/b] Whispers in the Moss will offer a full-scale JRPG experience. Estimating the amount of gameplay is challenging, but I expect the game to have at least 20 hours of gameplay for the type of player who likes to explore, complete optional stuff et cetera. To give you some idea, I recently made a speedthrough attempt through the game's main story. I used the New Game+ mode, so my characters started at a high level and I was able to complete each battle with ease, I didn't do any exploring, I didn't complete any optional stuff and I skipped through all the dialogue. It took me almost exactly 2 hours to complete the game in this way.
[*][b]HELP SPREAD THE WORD![/b] As a part-time solo developer, I've been focusing heavily on getting the game finished. I haven't been able to put much resources on the marketing, so help is needed! If you like what you're seeing, please spread the word. If you're familiar with some niche communities or groups that might be interested in the game, let me know!
[/list]

That's it for today. Take care, everybody!
[i]- T / Uncultured Games[/i]
